title: The Galo Negro: from the Munhango station to the grave at Lopitanga
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Munhango, birth beside the Benguela line
stops.date_confidence: attested; coordinates corrected to the OSM/Nominatim position for Munhango, the three research lenses having given three different pins, one of them 55 km west of the town
stops.campa: On the Benguela line, where the rails run east from the ocean toward the copper of Katanga, the stationmaster Lote Malheiro Savimbi keeps the signals and preaches for the Evangelical Congregational Church of Angola. His son Jonas Malheiro is born beside the track on the third of August. The line carries other people's ore out of Africa along the axis Cecil Rhodes wanted for his own railway. The boy will spend his life fighting over what the rails carry and who collects at the far end. Portugal calls the territory an overseas province and counts the family among its natives.
suggested_refs: The Munhango station on the Caminho de Ferro de Benguela, Bié Province

stops.name: Dondi, the Currie Institute
stops.date_confidence: traditional: attendance c.1946-1951 rests on Bridgland (1986), which was not read directly; month and day defaulted. The province was corrected from Bié to Huambo
stops.campa: The Congregationalist mission at Dondi runs the Currie Institute, the largest Protestant school open to Ovimbundu children under Portuguese rule. Here the stationmaster's son learns Latin and scripture, and learns to hold a room, inside a network answerable to American churches rather than to Lisbon. The colonial state licenses assimilados one at a time and keeps the count low. The mission schools a generation the state never licensed, and the men it teaches owe their letters to foreigners Lisbon cannot expel from the territory.
suggested_refs: The Dondi mission complex and Currie Institute, Cachiungo, Huambo Province
sources: Fred Bridgland, 'Jonas Savimbi: A Key to Africa' (1986), via the research pool

stops.name: Lisbon, medicine on a mission scholarship
stops.date_confidence: attested by inference: Wikipedia gives 'at age 24', which places the award in 1958 for a man born 3 August 1934; the pool's date of 1950 is discarded and month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: At twenty-four he arrives in the metropole on a scholarship from the United Church of Christ, an American Protestant body, to read medicine at the University of Lisbon. Perhaps a few dozen Angolans hold university places in Portugal in these years, and the PIDE keeps a file on each of them. He attends lectures on anatomy and meets, in cafes and rented rooms, students who will lead three rival movements home. The empire has gathered its colonial subjects into one city in order to civilise them, and has assembled its own opposition in a single street.
suggested_refs: The Faculty of Medicine of the University of Lisbon, and the PIDE files on colonial students

stops.name: Lausanne, out of Portugal
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: no reachable source gives the year of the flight. Bracketed 1959-1960 from the August 1960 Fribourg anchor, since he only reached Lisbon in 1958; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: With the secret police tightening around the colonial students, Savimbi crosses into Switzerland and puts a border between himself and the empire. Lausanne takes him in; medicine falls away. At Fribourg he enrols in the social and political sciences and never goes back to the anatomy lectures. No source records the month he left, or the name of whoever arranged the crossing. He is twenty-five or twenty-six, and he keeps a student's registration from here on while doing a politician's work.
suggested_refs: The Swiss universities as refuge for lusophone African students under PIDE surveillance

stops.name: Fribourg, the meeting with Holden Roberto
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; day defaulted
stops.campa: In a Swiss university town in August, two Angolans meet who will spend forty years unable to work together. Holden Roberto runs the UPA out of Léopoldville and needs educated men; Savimbi has the degrees, the languages, and the Ovimbundu south that Roberto's Bakongo movement cannot reach. Roberto offers him a place in a nationalism already organised. Savimbi takes it. The alliance lasts four years. The rupture that ends it outlasts Portuguese rule, and it outlasts the Cold War that comes after.
suggested_refs: The University of Fribourg, where Savimbi read social sciences

stops.name: Kampala, the speech for UDEAN
stops.date_confidence: attested for the Kampala speech and the meeting with Tom Mboya, both late September 1960; day defaulted. The Jomo Kenyatta encounter that the quotation presupposes cannot fall in this month, Kenyatta being in restricted exile at Lodwar until 1961, and the contradiction is left unresolved
stops.campa: He travels down to Kampala at the end of September and speaks for the UDEAN students on the liberation of Angola, his first appearance before an audience of Africans about to govern themselves. Tom Mboya hears him. On the tour he watches independence being scheduled rather than demanded, and watches which delegations get a hearing: the ones with a foreign patron standing behind them. He returns to Switzerland with contacts in four capitals and a name that arrives before he does.
stops.quote_source: Savimbi to the French press, given as late September 1960 and translated in the source as 'I was convinced by Kenyatta', as quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Jonas Savimbi'; the original press item was not reached and the date conflicts with Kenyatta's confinement at Lodwar
suggested_refs: The UDEAN student network and the 1960 pan-African student circuit

stops.name: New York, the case put to the United Nations
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; day defaulted
stops.campa: The nationalist carries his case to the building on the East River where empires are argued over annually. Portugal insists Angola is not a colony but a province, and therefore not the Assembly's business; the petitioners insist otherwise. Three years later Che Guevara will stand at this same rostrum and name the Congo and Vietnam in one breath. Savimbi is not yet anybody's client. He is a student with a briefcase asking a chamber of governments to notice a war running in the Angolan north since February.
suggested_refs: UN General Assembly debates on Portuguese overseas territories, 1961
sources: che_guevara.journey.json (UN General Assembly stop, canonical pin)

stops.name: Lucerne, secretary-general of the UNEA
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; day defaulted
stops.campa: At a meeting in Lucerne the Angolan students in Europe make him secretary-general of the UNEA. It is a small office over a scattered constituency, a few hundred young men studying in Lisbon, Paris, Geneva and Léopoldville, and it is exactly the machine he needs. The men who will staff UNITA's first bush administration meet one another in these years, in Swiss lecture halls, on stipends from churches and foreign ministries. He is assembling a cadre before he has a movement to put it in.
suggested_refs: The União Nacional dos Estudantes Angolanos (UNEA), founded among exile students in Europe

segments.name: The Break, Peking Doctrine, and Muangai

stops.name: Léopoldville, foreign minister of the GRAE
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date and the post; the seat of government is inferred from the FNLA's base, Wikipedia not naming it. The pool's acronym 'GREA' is corrected to GRAE
stops.campa: Roberto proclaims a revolutionary government of Angola in exile, the GRAE, and hands the foreign ministry to Savimbi, who is twenty-seven. He tours the newly independent capitals arguing the FNLA's claim to recognition and obtains it from a good many of them. Inside the exile capital he watches the government do very little else: no offensive into Angola, no recruitment in the Ovimbundu south, a treasury spent on rents and motorcars in Léopoldville. He keeps the post for two years and spends the second one planning his exit.
suggested_refs: The Governo Revolucionário de Angola no Exílio (GRAE), proclaimed 3 April 1962

stops.name: Beijing, asking for a sponsor
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Having concluded that Roberto's war is an office, Savimbi goes looking for a sponsor who will arm a movement that does not exist yet. Peking receives him. The Chinese are competing with Moscow for the loyalty of African insurgents, and Moscow has already chosen the MPLA; a rival Angolan with no Soviet ties is worth a hearing and worth rifles. He asks for weapons and training, and the Chinese offer both, with the doctrine that goes with them. The MPLA will be supplied by one communist capital and UNITA, at the start, by the other.
suggested_refs: Chinese support for African liberation movements in the Sino-Soviet split

stops.name: Nanjing, the doctrine of protracted war
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the training is standard in the biographical literature but the academy and the exact months vary by source; Bridgland (1986) not read directly. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: For some months in China he is put through the People's Liberation Army's course in guerrilla organisation: the political commissar beside the commander, the party branch inside the company, the peasant base area that feeds an army the state cannot find. It is the system Mao Zedong assembled at Sanwan in 1927 and exported to Africa for a decade. Savimbi will run it in Portuguese and in Umbundu, against a colonial army and then against a Marxist one that learned the same lessons from Moscow.
suggested_refs: PLA training of African liberation cadres, mid-1960s
sources: Fred Bridgland, 'Jonas Savimbi: A Key to Africa' (1986), via the research pool

stops.name: Lausanne, the doctorate
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He returns to Switzerland and finishes what he began, taking his doctorate in law and political science at Lausanne. The man who will be photographed for thirty years in fatigues writes a thesis and defends it. He speaks Portuguese, French, English and Umbundu, and will use all four to explain Angola to whichever capital is listening. The degree is the last thing he acquires in Europe. The following year he is on foot in Moxico province with two hundred men and no state at all.
suggested_refs: The University of Lausanne doctorate in law and political science, 1965

stops.name: Muangai, the founding of UNITA
stops.date_confidence: attested for date, place and the count of some 200 delegates; coordinates corrected to the OSM position for Muangai, now Lutuai, the pool's two pins lying 60 km and 180 km away
stops.campa: Two hundred delegates come in on foot through the eastern bush to a place called Muangai, eighty kilometres south of Luena, and on the thirteenth of March they found the União Nacional para a Independência Total de Angola. Savimbi and António da Costa Fernandes write it out: total independence, no partition of the country with anyone, no exile government, the war to be fought inside Angola by Angolans who live there. The MPLA has Luanda and the Soviets, the FNLA has Léopoldville and the Americans. UNITA has Moxico.
suggested_refs: The founding congress at Muangai (Lutuai), Moxico Province, 13 March 1966

stops.name: Teixeira de Sousa, the first attack
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date and for eastern Angola; the identification of Teixeira de Sousa (Luau) as the target rests on Bridgland (1986), not read directly
stops.campa: On Christmas Day UNITA cuts the Benguela railway at the border town of Teixeira de Sousa, its first action in the war it has just declared. The line is the artery the chartered-company generation of Cecil Rhodes dreamed of and Portugal completed, hauling Katangan and Zambian copper to the Atlantic. Savimbi attacks the colonial economy at the one point where it is a single steel thread eighteen hundred kilometres long. Portugal loses freight; Zambia, whose copper rides the same rails, loses patience faster than Lisbon does.
suggested_refs: The Benguela railway at Luau (Teixeira de Sousa), on the Katanga frontier
sources: Fred Bridgland, 'Jonas Savimbi: A Key to Africa' (1986), via the research pool

stops.name: Lusaka, Kaunda closes the sanctuary
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: dated 1967-1968 in the standard accounts, which rest on Bridgland (1986); month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Kenneth Kaunda has given the young movement houses in Lusaka and a border to cross. He also has a landlocked country whose entire copper export runs down the line UNITA keeps blowing up. When the attacks continue he closes the sanctuary and expels the leadership, and the movement that has just declared itself the only Angolan force fighting inside Angola discovers that it now truly is: no rear base, no patron, no capital. Savimbi walks back into Moxico and stays in the bush for seven years.
suggested_refs: Zambia's rupture with UNITA over the Benguela railway attacks
sources: Fred Bridgland, 'Jonas Savimbi: A Key to Africa' (1986), via the research pool

stops.name: Luanda, the flag comes down
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool's 'August 1975' for UNITA's withdrawal south is corrected to July 1975 per Wikipedia, 'Angolan Civil War'
stops.campa: At midnight on the eleventh of November the Portuguese flag comes down and nobody agrees on what replaces it. The MPLA holds the capital, having forced the FNLA out of it in July while UNITA withdrew south to the Ovimbundu plateau. Cuban troops are already landing; Fidel Castro has decided in Havana that the Angolan revolution will be defended by Cubans, and thousands of them are ashore before the year ends. Angola is independent for one day before the war between its liberators becomes the only war there is.
suggested_refs: The Alvor Agreement and the Portuguese withdrawal of 11 November 1975

stops.name: Huambo, the Democratic People's Republic of Angola
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool credited the proclamation to UNITA alone, corrected to the FNLA and UNITA jointly per Wikipedia, 'Democratic People's Republic of Angola'
stops.campa: On the same day, four hundred kilometres inland, the FNLA and UNITA proclaim a Democratic People's Republic of Angola at Huambo, with Savimbi and Roberto briefly inside one government again. Two states with two capitals claim the same country. The Organisation of African Unity that Haile Selassie founded at Addis Ababa in 1963 must now choose which Angola to seat, and it chooses Luanda. The Huambo republic lasts weeks. Savimbi will spend twenty-seven years trying to reverse a recognition decided in an Ethiopian conference hall.
suggested_refs: The Democratic People's Republic of Angola, proclaimed at Huambo, 11 November 1975

stops.name: Jamba, the bush capital
stops.date_confidence: attested for the place; coordinates corrected from a pin some 200 km north-west, and the headquarters period corrected to 1976-1999 per Wikipedia, 'Jamba, Cuando Cubango'. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: In the far south-east, in sand country near the Namibian and Zambian borders where nothing grows and no road runs, Savimbi builds a capital. Jamba has schools, a hospital, workshops, a landing strip and a population that calls him the Galo Negro, the black cockerel. Foreign journalists reach it only by his invitation and by South African aircraft. For sixteen years it is the seat of a state that appears on no map: courts, a standing army, a currency of sorts, and one man who is its president and its only law.
suggested_refs: Jamba, Cuando Cubango, UNITA's headquarters until its capture in December 1999
sources: Fred Bridgland, 'Jonas Savimbi: A Key to Africa' (1986), via the research pool

stops.name: Luanda, the party declares itself Marxist-Leninist
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: The MPLA declares itself a Marxist-Leninist vanguard party and renames itself accordingly. The declaration settles Angola's place in the world ledger and hands Savimbi the argument he will sell in Washington for a decade: that his war is not a quarrel over a former colony but the southern front of the global one. Government offensives in 1977 and 1978, with Soviet planning and Cuban troops, drive south to finish UNITA and fail to find him. Failing to find him becomes, for twenty-five years, the government's chronic condition.
suggested_refs: The MPLA's first congress and its adoption of Marxism-Leninism, December 1977

stops.name: Kinshasa, Mobutu's transit route
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction of a standing arrangement dated 1975-1988 in the historiography; a single year and a default month and day are used for the pin
stops.campa: Mobutu Sese Seko renames his country Zaire and rents it out. Arms from South Africa and the United States come through Kinshasa and down to the Angolan border, and Savimbi becomes a familiar visitor at a palace where anti-communism is a commodity with a price list. Ten years earlier Che Guevara had crossed this same country in the other direction, trying to open a front against the men Washington was paying. The Congo is the hinge of both wars, and no Angolan movement is supplied without someone in Kinshasa taking a cut.
suggested_refs: The Zaire supply corridor for UNITA, described in Gleijeses and Wright
sources: Piero Gleijeses and George Wright on the Zaire corridor, via the research pool

stops.name: Pretoria, the patron across the border
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the alliance is documented, individual Pretoria visits are asserted in secondary sources only. Canonical pin inherited from the atlas; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: The apartheid government is now his principal patron: training, artillery, air cover, and a border it will cross at will. South Africa is fighting SWAPO in Namibia and the Cubans in Angola, and UNITA is the infantry it prefers not to bury at home. In this same capital Nelson Mandela is a prisoner serving a life sentence; released, he will fly to Tripoli to thank Muammar Gaddafi for backing the struggle against the men who armed Savimbi. Two Africas are defended from one city, and only one of them still exists in 1994.
suggested_refs: The South Africa-UNITA alliance of the 1980s
sources: Cold War Angola historiography, via the research pool
muammar_gaddafi.journey.json (Mandela in Tripoli stop, canonical Pretoria pin)

stops.name: Washington, the Clark Amendment repealed
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; day defaulted
stops.campa: Congress repeals the Clark Amendment, the 1976 law that had forbidden covert American military aid to any Angolan faction after the last such programme collapsed in scandal. The door opens; the Heritage Foundation has pushed at it for years, and Savimbi will thank the foundation from a Washington podium in October 1989. A lobbying firm begins drawing some six hundred thousand dollars a year to keep UNITA's name clean in the capital. The guerrilla who founded a movement in the bush at Muangai now has a public relations budget.
suggested_refs: The repeal of the Clark Amendment, July 1985

stops.name: The White House, Reagan receives him
stops.date_confidence: attested; the day is supplied by the geography lens where the chronology lens gave only the year
stops.campa: Ronald Reagan receives him in the White House, and the man from Jamba appears on American television fluent, quotable, and described as a freedom fighter. The Reagan Doctrine needs an African exhibit and Savimbi is the best-spoken one available. Covert aid resumes, Stinger missiles among it. He has now been armed in turn by China, by South Africa and by the United States, and has fought the Portuguese empire, the Soviet Union and Cuba with the proceeds. Nobody in the room speaks Umbundu.
stops.quote: a victory that electrifies the world
stops.quote_source: Ronald Reagan on UNITA, remarks following the White House meeting of January 1986, as quoted in the Wikipedia article 'Jonas Savimbi'; the original transcript was not reached
suggested_refs: The Reagan-Savimbi White House meeting, 30 January 1986

stops.name: Mavinga, the gate to Jamba
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1985 and 1987-1988 offensives against Mavinga; a single year is used for the pin and month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: Mavinga is a strip of red earth and a runway in the middle of nothing, and it is the gate to Jamba. Soviet planners in Luanda draw the same arrow on the map every other year: south down the Cuito, across the Lomba, take Mavinga, then take Jamba and the war is over. FAPLA tries it in 1985 and is stopped. It tries again in 1987 with more armour and more advisers. Everything that happens on the Lomba and at Cuito Cuanavale happens because this airstrip is worth more than the province it stands in.
suggested_refs: Mavinga, UNITA's forward logistics town in Cuando Cubango

stops.name: Cuito Cuanavale, the offensive begins
stops.date_confidence: attested for the start date and the coordinates, which match the article's 15 degrees 09 minutes 50 seconds south, 19 degrees 10 minutes 23 seconds east
stops.campa: FAPLA's brigades move out from Cuito Cuanavale on the fourteenth of August toward Mavinga, with Cuban advisers, Soviet armour and air cover. South Africa commits ground forces to stop them and UNITA supplies the infantry that knows the ground. What begins as one more dry-season offensive turns into the largest conventional battle fought in Africa since 1945, over a river crossing and a runway in a province with almost nobody living in it. Roughly three thousand UNITA fighters will be killed before it ends.
suggested_refs: The FAPLA offensive of August 1987 and the SADF intervention

stops.name: The Lomba River, the 47th Brigade destroyed
stops.date_confidence: attested as the opening of the Lomba River fighting, which ran 6 September to 7 October 1987; the pool dated the destruction of 47 Brigade to this day, whereas the article places that on 3 October 1987
stops.campa: South of the town the FAPLA columns have to cross the Lomba, and on the sixth of September the fighting on its banks begins. It runs a month. On the third of October the 47th Brigade is destroyed on the river line, caught between South African armour and UNITA infantry with the water at its back. The offensive toward Mavinga stops there and never resumes. Savimbi's men have fought a set-piece battle beside a conventional army, which is not the war he was trained for at Nanjing and not a war he can fight alone.
suggested_refs: The Lomba River engagements, 6 September to 7 October 1987

stops.name: Rundu, the columns come from Namibia
stops.date_confidence: attested for the role of Rundu across the 1987-1988 campaign; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Across the border in Namibia, the South African Defence Force runs its columns north from Rundu on the Okavango, into a country it is not at war with, to relieve a movement it does not officially arm. The logistics of Savimbi's greatest battle belong to a foreign general staff. When Pretoria decides in 1988 that the price of Cuito Cuanavale is higher than Namibia is worth, the columns go home and the border closes behind them, and no amount of American money replaces what used to cross it.
suggested_refs: Rundu, South African staging point on the Okavango

stops.name: Cuito Cuanavale, both sides claim it
stops.date_confidence: attested for the end date; the outcome is disputed and both claims are reported rather than adjudicated, the pool's description of a UNITA victory being softened accordingly
stops.campa: On the twenty-third of March the fighting stops. The South Africans and UNITA have halted the advance on Mavinga; the Cubans and FAPLA hold their ground east of the Cuito river and are not destroyed. Both sides declare a victory and both are believed at home. Havana reads the outcome as the end of South African power in the region and negotiates accordingly; within the year Pretoria signs away Namibia and agrees to leave Angola. Savimbi wins his battle and loses, in the same season, the army that fought it beside him.
suggested_refs: The disputed outcome of Cuito Cuanavale and the New York Accords of December 1988

stops.name: Washington, the letter from a president-elect
stops.date_confidence: attested to the date of reporting; the pool had placed this pledge at a 1990 meeting, and it is corrected to a letter written before the inauguration
stops.campa: Before he is sworn in, George Bush writes to Savimbi promising all appropriate and effective assistance, which an aide explains to the Washington Post means the covert military aid then running at some fifteen million dollars a year. The letter is reported on the twelfth of January. In December of the same year Bush sends an army into Panama to seize Manuel Noriega, an anti-communist client who had outlived his usefulness. Savimbi reads the American commitment as permanent. It has about eighteen months to run.
stops.quote_source: George H. W. Bush, written pledge to Savimbi before taking office, reported in the Washington Post, 'Bush Assures Savimbi of U.S. Support', 12 January 1989, and in the New York Times, David Rampe, January 1989
suggested_refs: The Bush letter of January 1989 and the covert aid programme it continued
sources: New York Times, David Rampe, January 1989

stops.name: Gbadolite, the first handshake
stops.date_confidence: attested; coordinates corrected from a pin roughly 800 km south, in the wrong half of the Congo, to the article's 4 degrees 17 minutes north, 21 degrees 01 minutes east
stops.campa: Mobutu assembles African heads of state at his marble palace in the northern Congolese forest, and Savimbi and José Eduardo dos Santos shake hands for the first time in front of them. There is a declaration and a ceasefire. There is no agreed text: the two men leave believing different things about whether Savimbi is to go into exile, and each says so publicly within weeks. The ceasefire dies before the year is out. Three months earlier he had told two American visitors what he thought of the year's other bargain.
stops.quote: There are a lot of loopholes in that agreement. The agreement is not good at all.
stops.quote_source: Savimbi to Michael Johns and Howard Phillips in Angola, March 1989, speaking of the New York Accords rather than of Gbadolite; published in Michael Johns, 'Savimbi's Elusive Victory in Angola', Human Events, 26 October 1989, which could not be read directly
suggested_refs: The Gbadolite Declaration of 22 June 1989 and its collapse
sources: contemporary press coverage of the Gbadolite summit

stops.name: Jamba, wounded twice in two months
stops.date_confidence: attested that he was wounded twice within two months in early 1990; no source gives the place, and UNITA's seat at Jamba is used as an approximate pin. Day defaulted
stops.campa: He is wounded twice in fighting inside two months, at fifty-five years old, still moving with his own columns. The Soviet Union is dissolving; Cuban troops are leaving on the schedule agreed in New York; the American aid that repeal of the Clark Amendment unlocked is becoming an embarrassment to a Washington no longer at war with Moscow. He will fly to Washington within months and be received by Bush at the White House. Every patron he has ever had is preparing, in these same two years, to stop paying.
suggested_refs: The winding down of superpower support for both Angolan sides, 1990-1991

stops.name: Bicesse, the accords signed outside Lisbon
stops.date_confidence: attested for date, signatories and the 152,000 demobilisation figure; the pin is moved from central Lisbon to Bicesse in Alcabideche, Cascais, about 25 km west, which is why the accords are equally called the Estoril Accords
stops.campa: At Bicesse, in Alcabideche outside Lisbon, Savimbi and dos Santos sign an agreement to end sixteen years of civil war: a ceasefire, demobilisation of some hundred and fifty-two thousand fighters into a single national army, and multi-party elections within eighteen months. Portugal, the United States and the Soviet Union stand behind it, the last useful thing those three do together. Neither army fully demobilises. Both keep their best units and their weapons caches, and each knows the other is doing it.
suggested_refs: The Bicesse (Estoril) Accords, 31 May 1991

stops.name: Luanda, campaigning as a civilian
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month of the campaign and the election of 29-30 September 1992; day defaulted
stops.campa: For the first time he campaigns in the capital as a civilian, in a suit, in a city he has never governed and has spent seventeen years besieging by proxy. Crowds come. The MPLA holds the state, the television, the oil revenue and the towns; UNITA holds the countryside and the memory of who burned it. Savimbi tells audiences that whoever wins the count should govern and that he will accept it. Four and a half million voters are registered in a country where nobody has ever voted.
suggested_refs: The 1992 Angolan general election campaign

stops.name: Huambo, the runoff refused
stops.date_confidence: attested for the vote shares and for the announcement of results on 17 October 1992; the sequence of the refusal is reconstruction, and the pool tagged it [R]
stops.campa: The count gives dos Santos 49.56 percent and Savimbi 40.07 percent, short of the majority the constitution requires, and orders a second round. United Nations observers call the election generally free and fair. Savimbi calls it fraud, refuses the runoff, and withdraws his generals from the army they had just joined. The runoff is never held; Angola waits until 2008 to vote again. He is fifty-eight. In one week he stakes everything he built in Europe and in the bush on a refusal to come second.
suggested_refs: The announcement of the 1992 results and the runoff that never took place

stops.name: Luanda, the Halloween killings
stops.date_confidence: attested for the dates and for the deaths of Chitunda and Salupeto Pena on 2 November; the casualty range is enormous and no source consulted narrows it, so it is reported as a range
stops.campa: Fighting breaks out in the capital on the thirtieth of October and runs three days. Government forces and armed civilians hunt UNITA members and supporters through Luanda; the vice-president of the movement, Jeremias Chitunda, and the senior advisor Elias Salupeto Pena are shot in the street on the second of November. Estimates of the dead run from several thousand to tens of thousands. Angolans call it the Halloween killings, and the war resumes at a scale the colonial one never reached.
suggested_refs: The Halloween Massacre in Luanda, 30 October to 1 November 1992
sources: Human Rights Watch and contemporary press accounts

stops.name: Huambo, fifty-five days
stops.date_confidence: attested for the siege of January to March 1993; Savimbi's personal presence during it is not confirmed by any source consulted and is left as a gap. Day defaulted
stops.campa: UNITA besieges Huambo, the second city of Angola and the town where it once proclaimed a republic, and takes it after fifty-five days of house-to-house fighting that leave the centre in ruins. The movement now holds perhaps two-thirds of the country and the diamond fields that pay for it, and no capital and no recognition. The United Nations imposes sanctions on UNITA for refusing the election result. Savimbi has traded international standing for territory, and territory is what he loses next.
suggested_refs: The 55-day siege of Huambo, 1993
sources: Contemporary press, UN and human rights reporting on the 1993 siege of Huambo

stops.name: Lusaka, the Protocol he does not sign
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool's placing of the rejected vice-presidency at this signing is corrected, dos Santos having offered it in 1995 and Savimbi having rejected it in August 1996
stops.campa: A second peace is signed at Lusaka: ceasefire, UNITA fighters into the national army and the police, cabinet seats and governorships for the movement. Savimbi does not come. The secretary-general Eugénio Manuvakola signs for UNITA and Foreign Minister Venâncio de Moura for the government, and the absence of the one signature that matters is noted in every account of the day. Dos Santos offers him the vice-presidency in 1995; he rejects it in August 1996, by which time the protocol is a fiction both sides maintain.
suggested_refs: The Lusaka Protocol, 20 November 1994
sources: UN documentation of the Lusaka Protocol

stops.name: Bailundo, the political headquarters
stops.date_confidence: attested for Bailundo as UNITA's political seat 1994-1999; a single date is used for the pin and the day is defaulted
stops.campa: With Jamba too exposed and Huambo lost again, the political headquarters moves to Bailundo, on the plateau above the old Ovimbundu kingdom whose name UNITA has always invoked. From here Savimbi runs a movement that is at once a political party with ministers in Luanda and an army that has not disarmed. He receives diplomats and United Nations envoys and misses every deadline they bring. The Protocol holds for four years in the sense that the shooting is intermittent rather than continuous.
suggested_refs: Bailundo, UNITA's political headquarters in the Lusaka Protocol years
sources: Contemporary press and UN reporting on UNITA's Bailundo headquarters

segments.name: The Last Column and the Grave

stops.name: Andulo, the military headquarters falls
stops.date_confidence: attested that Bailundo and Andulo fell in October 1999; the pool's account of the offensive omitted Andulo entirely and paired Jamba with Bailundo instead. Day defaulted
stops.campa: North-east of Bailundo, Andulo is the other half of the arrangement: the military headquarters, the airstrips that bring in fuel and take out diamonds, the workshops, the family. In December 1998 the Protocol collapses outright and the government stops pretending; in October 1999 Operation Restore Order takes Andulo and Bailundo in the same month. The state UNITA has maintained for a quarter of a century inside Angola loses its capitals, and the man who founded it goes back into the bush at sixty-five.
suggested_refs: Operação Restauro and the fall of Andulo and Bailundo, October 1999
sources: Contemporary press and UN reporting on the fall of Andulo and Bailundo

stops.name: Jamba, taken on Christmas Eve
stops.date_confidence: attested for the capture date per Wikipedia, 'Jamba, Cuando Cubango'; the pool had dated the loss of Jamba to the October offensive
stops.campa: On Christmas Eve, thirty-three years after UNITA's first attack on the Benguela railway, government forces walk into Jamba. The schools, the hospital, the runway, the bush capital that foreign correspondents flew into by South African arrangement to interview a president with no country: all of it taken in a day, against little resistance, because there is no longer an army there to hold it. The conventional UNITA that fought at Cuito Cuanavale is finished. What is left is what Savimbi began with, and less.
suggested_refs: The capture of Jamba, 24 December 1999

stops.name: Eastern Moxico, the mobile column
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: no camp location from these years is documented anywhere consulted, and an approximate eastern Moxico pin is used with a defaulted date inside the 1999-2002 span
stops.campa: He goes east into the forests of Moxico, the province where he founded the movement, with a column that moves camp every few days. No fixed base, no airstrip, no foreign patron: South Africa is governed by the men it once jailed, Washington recognises Luanda, the diamond trade is under sanction. He is a few hundred guerrillas and a radio, in country he has known since 1966. The government fields tracking units with foreign equipment and hunts him for two and a half years.
suggested_refs: UNITA's return to guerrilla warfare in Moxico, 1999-2002
sources: Press coverage of Savimbi's final years, via the research pool

stops.name: Lucusse, the firefight on the Luvuei
stops.date_confidence: attested for date and wound count; the location is given in contemporary press as the Luvuei river near Lucusse, and the pool's 'Chambinga' is deleted, that ground lying 600 km away in Cuando Cubango
stops.campa: On the twenty-second of February a government tracking unit catches the column on the Luvuei river near Lucusse, in the province where UNITA was founded, and kills him in the firefight. He takes fifteen bullets, to head, throat, upper body and legs. State television shows the body because Angolans have stopped believing that he can die; for thirty-six years the army has announced his death and been wrong. A brigadier tells the Portuguese news agency, three days later, how the president of UNITA was found.
stops.quote: he had died like a soldier, with a gun in his hand
stops.quote_source: Brigadier Simão Carlitos Wala of the Angolan Armed Forces to the Lusa agency, reported by BBC News, 'Savimbi died with gun in hand', 25 February 2002
suggested_refs: The Luvuei river near Lucusse, Moxico Province, site of the firefight of 22 February 2002

stops.name: Luena, the grave and the ceasefire
stops.date_confidence: attested for the burial at Luena and for the April 2002 Luena Memorandum; the day of burial is not given in the sources consulted and is defaulted
stops.campa: The body is buried at Luena, the provincial capital, in the main cemetery under a bronze plaque, on ground the government controls and UNITA is not permitted to visit. Six weeks later, in the same town, the movement's surviving commanders and the government sign the Luena Memorandum of Understanding: ceasefire, amnesty, demobilisation. In August UNITA disbands its armed wing and becomes a political party. Twenty-seven years of war end within six months of one man's death.
suggested_refs: The Luena Memorandum of Understanding, April 2002

stops.name: Luena, the tomb broken
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day
stops.campa: Members of the MPLA youth wing break into the cemetery at Luena and damage the grave. Four are arrested and administratively punished. Angola has held no election since 1992 and will hold one in September; the party that has governed since independence is asking the country to forget a man it cannot leave alone. There is no statue of Savimbi anywhere, no museum, no state monument. For six years the only object in Angola carrying his name has been a plaque, and it has just been broken.
suggested_refs: The vandalising of Savimbi's tomb at Luena, 3 January 2008

stops.name: Lopitanga, the return to Andulo
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by Portuguese Wikipedia; the geography lens gave 25 October 2019 and is overruled by two other lenses and the source. Lopitanga returns no gazetteer entry, so the Andulo coordinate is used as approximate
stops.campa: Seventeen years after the firefight the remains are exhumed at Luena, identified by DNA, and carried to Lopitanga in the Andulo municipality, the ancestral ground his family had asked for since 2002. João Lourenço permits the transfer; Isaías Samakuva declares UNITA's mourning at an end. The village returns no entry in any gazetteer. The Galo Negro is buried a short drive from the headquarters the army took in 1999, in the province where he was born, by a government that spent a quarter of a century trying to find him.
suggested_refs: The reburial at Lopitanga, Andulo, 1 June 2019, following the agreement of 30 May 2019
sources: Reuters, AFP and BBC coverage of the 2019 reburial
